```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.6,
  fig.height = 4.8, dpi = 144, out.width = "100%")
library(postrank)
source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank",
  mustWork = TRUE), local = TRUE)
analysis <- load_or_compute("case_cde_12")
case <- pr_case_cde
criterion <- case$input$criterion_ids
stopifnot(length(criterion) == 1L, identical(analysis$input, case$input),
  identical(case$input$event, "higher_priority"), analysis$fit$incumbent_validated)
fmt <- function(z, digits = 3L) formatC(z, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(z, digits = 1L) paste0(fmt(100 * z, digits), "%")
count <- function(z) format(z, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
sci <- function(z) formatC(z, digits = 2L, format = "e")
n_school <- nrow(case$units)
state_n <- case$reference$statewide$schools
source_year <- sub(".*publication ([0-9]{4}).*", "\\1", case$provenance$source_version)
school_year <- sub(".*academic year ([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}).*", "\\1", case$provenance$source_version)
minimum_n <- as.integer(sub(".*n>=([0-9]+).*", "\\1", case$provenance$source_frame))
prior_lambda <- as.numeric(sub(".*lambda=([0-9.]+)\\. Independent.*", "\\1",
  case$provenance$conditioning))
strata <- dim(case$provenance$full_frame_stratum_counts)
level <- case$input$summaries$level
ev <- analysis$evaluation
grades <- get_grades(analysis)
profile <- get_profile(analysis)
tau <- analysis$settings$tau
cap <- analysis$settings$G_max
middle_grade <- sort(unique(grades))[ceiling(length(unique(grades)) / 2)]
middle_ids <- names(grades)[grades == middle_grade]
P <- case$input$corrected_probabilities[, , 1L]
mid <- P[middle_ids, middle_ids, drop = FALSE]
best <- which(mid == max(mid, na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1L, ]
strong_ids <- c(rownames(mid)[best[1L]], colnames(mid)[best[2L]])
strong_probability <- mid[best[1L], best[2L]]
state <- case$reference$statewide$metrics
state_primary <- state[state$method == "posterior_mean", ]
qcheck <- case$reference$quadrature$checks
```

School accountability reports often order schools by their observed
absence rates. Such an ordering requires directional comparisons even when
nearby rates are difficult to distinguish. We use chronic absenteeism to
illustrate a one-criterion analysis in which `postrank` assigns schools to
ordered grades and withholds comparisons within grades.

The target is the current chronic-absence probability, with lower values
receiving higher priority. This target concerns neither a school's causal
effect on attendance nor the California School Dashboard's combination of
current level and change. Both would require additional information.

The posterior input and optimized grading were prepared in advance. The
article reads these results and evaluates fixed reports, without refitting
a model or executing an optimizer during rendering. An optional call is
provided for recomputing the small example.

## Schools, observations and posterior distribution {#start-with-schools-counts-and-a-posterior}

The source study uses the frozen `r source_year` Dashboard publication for
school year `r school_year`. Its chronic-absence frame contains
`r count(state_n)` elementary-type, non-alternative schools with usable
all-students counts and current-year denominators of at least `r minimum_n`;
charter schools are included. This is the study's eligible frame, rather than
every school in California. The denominator is the indicator's eligible
student-school count, so summing it across schools need not count unique
students.

The bundled example contains `r n_school` schools, selected deterministically
from the cross-classification of `r strata[1L]` observed-rate rank groups and
`r strata[2L]` denominator rank groups, with one school per cell. This
selection distributes the example across the source frame but does not
constitute a representative sample for estimating statewide prevalence.

The source is the [CDE chronic-absenteeism download collection](https://www.cde.ca.gov/ta/ac/cm/chronicdatafiles.asp).
The compact CDE-derived input preserves source attribution and documented
transformations. The dataset help, `?pr_case_cde`, retains the source
details and links to the [CDE copyright statement](https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp).
The installed DATA-NOTICE distinguishes historical preparation records from
the current distribution scope.

```{r input}
library(postrank)
case <- pr_case_cde
input <- case$input
schools <- case$units

# Short display names; the original CDS identifiers stay in the data.
school_labels <- setNames(paste("School", LETTERS[seq_len(nrow(schools))]),
  schools[["entity_id"]])
criterion_labels <- setNames("Lower chronic absence (-p)", input[["criterion_ids"]])
```

```{r observed-table, echo=FALSE}
observed <- data.frame(
  School = unname(school_labels[schools$entity_id]),
  `CDS identifier` = schools$entity_id,
  `Chronic-absence count` = schools$chronic_absent_count,
  `Eligible count` = schools$eligible_count,
  `Observed rate` = pct(schools$observed_rate, 2L), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(observed, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Observed counts for the teaching subset. Rates are y/n; CDS identifiers retain leading zeros.")
```

The observed proportion `y/n` enters a working model in which each school's
count is binomial conditional on its current absence probability `p`.
An empirical Bayes distribution `G` was estimated from the full
`r count(state_n)`-school frame. This estimated distribution is retained for
the selected schools, rather than refitted to the small selected sample.
Observed proportions and posterior means are consequently distinct
quantities. The prior fit uses regularization `lambda =` `r prior_lambda`,
a model-fitting parameter distinct from the reporting cost `tau` below.

The prior has `r length(case$reference$frozen_posterior$prior_bin_masses)`
continuous bins, with uniform density within each bin. After observing a
school's counts, its posterior within a bin is a
`Beta(y + 1, n - y + 1)` distribution truncated to that bin. The school's
posterior combines these components with its posterior bin probabilities.
Evaluating the bin centers as discrete atoms would change this law. The
supplied means, intervals and comparisons all use the continuous version.

Posterior uncertainty is conditional on the estimated `G`: school
probabilities vary under the working model, while `G` is held fixed.
Uncertainty in estimating `G` is therefore omitted. The analysis also remains
conditional on the binomial assumptions, which may not capture every source
of variation in school attendance.

## Target direction and reporting loss {#orient-the-criterion-and-choose-the-report}

Since `postrank` assigns higher priority to larger targets, we define
`theta = -p`. Larger target values then correspond to lower chronic-absence
probabilities, and grade 1 has highest priority. The sign specifies the
direction of comparison; the underlying probability remains nonnegative.
A favorable comparison of school `i` with school `j` has probability
`Pr(p_i < p_j)`, equivalently `Pr(theta_i > theta_j)`.

The supplied comparison probabilities were calculated by numerical
integration. They consequently have no associated posterior draw count or
chain diagnostics. The continuous posterior assigns probability zero to
exact equality of distinct schools' targets. A shared grade nevertheless
withholds a comparison, without making a claim about equality of the school
probabilities.

The analysis permits at most `r cap` grades and assigns loss
`r fmt(tau, 2L)` to withholding a school pair, relative to loss one for a
wrong-direction disclosure. All unordered school pairs receive equal
weight. The single criterion has weight one, which may be omitted from the
function call.

The optional call below recomputes the small grading from the prepared
probabilities using HiGHS. It neither estimates a posterior nor executes
during document rendering.

```{r optional-solve, eval=FALSE}
analysis <- postrank(
  input,
  tau = .20, G_max = 3L,
  level = .90,
  backend = "highs",
  control = list(time_limit = 30, threads = 1L),
  fragility = FALSE
)
```

For any proposed report, let `M` be all unordered pairs, `N` the disclosed
pairs, and `E` the sum of posterior wrong-direction probabilities over those
disclosed pairs. Its expected loss is

`R = [E + tau * (M - N)] / M`.

Thus `tau` specifies a cost for withholding, rather than an error-rate
constraint. The grade cap requires a joint choice of ordered groups; separate
threshold decisions for individual pairs need not form an admissible report.
The at-most constraint permits fewer grades when they minimize loss.

## Grades and posterior uncertainty {#read-the-chosen-grades-and-their-uncertainty}

The prepared solution uses `r ev$G` grades. A basic result table contains
the original entity identifiers and their grades:

```{r grades-code, results='hide'}
grade_table <- as.data.frame(analysis)
```

```{r grade-table, echo=FALSE}
grade_groups <- lapply(sort(unique(grades)), function(g) {
  ids <- names(grades)[grades == g]
  data.frame(Grade = g, Schools = length(ids),
    Members = paste(unname(school_labels[ids]), collapse = ", "))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, grade_groups), row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "The prepared grading. Smaller grade numbers have higher priority; membership within a grade leaves comparisons unordered.")
```

The report card displays the selected groups and supplied
`r fmt(100 * level, 0L)`% marginal posterior intervals. Values closer to zero
on the oriented target scale indicate lower absence probabilities. Schools
are ordered within grades by posterior mean on this scale. The intervals
refer to individual schools and have no simultaneous coverage interpretation
for the report. Grade selection uses the decision loss rather than interval
overlap.

```{r card, fig.height=5.8, fig.cap=paste0("Posterior means and ", format(100 * level), "% equal-tail marginal intervals for theta = -p, conditional on the estimated statewide G. All selected schools are shown; short names refer to the observed-count table.")}
postrank_plot_report_card(
  analysis, order = "mean", order_by = input$criterion_ids,
  max_rows = nrow(schools), ncol = 1L,
  entity_labels = school_labels, criterion_labels = criterion_labels
)
```

For the negative target, the supplied mean is `-E[p]` and the interval
endpoints are `-q.95(p)` and `-q.05(p)`, in that order. Requesting
`level = .90` uses these retained summaries. A different interval level
would require additional posterior summaries; it cannot be recovered from
the stored endpoints alone.

```{r profile-code, results='hide'}
profile <- get_profile(analysis)
profile[c("E", "E_over_N", "E_over_M", "risk")]
```

Of the `r count(ev$M)` possible pairs, the report discloses
`r count(ev$N)` (`r pct(ev$disclosure_rate)`) and withholds
`r count(ev$M - ev$N)`. Its expected wrong-direction count is
`r fmt(unname(ev$E), 5L)`, giving an expected error proportion of
`r pct(profile$E_over_N, 4L)` among disclosed pairs. Dividing by all
pairs instead gives `r pct(profile$E_over_M, 4L)`. These are posterior
expectations, not observed counts of mistakes in future attendance data.

The total risk is `r fmt(ev$primary_risk, 6L)`. Withholding accounts for
`r fmt(tau * (ev$M - ev$N) / ev$M, 6L)`, whereas disclosed directional errors
contribute `r fmt(profile$E_over_M, 6L)`. Most of the risk therefore arises
from withheld comparisons. The expected error proportion among disclosed
pairs must be interpreted in relation to the extent of withholding.

The prepared solver status is `r analysis$fit$status$normalized`. Its
reported lower bound is `r fmt(analysis$fit$objective$risk_lower_bound, 6L)`
and its numerical risk gap is `r sci(analysis$fit$objective$risk_absolute_gap)`.
That gap concerns optimization of the supplied coefficients. It does not
measure posterior uncertainty, model accuracy or the error in numerical
integration.

## Pairwise support and withheld comparisons {#a-withheld-pair-can-still-have-a-clear-direction}

The relation map represents the selected report. Gray cells indicate
withheld comparisons and colored cells indicate the row school's disclosed
higher priority. One triangle is displayed so that each unordered pair
appears once.

```{r relations, fig.height=5.4, fig.cap="Selected pair relations for the same prepared grading. Gray cells withhold comparisons and do not assert equal absence probabilities."}
postrank_plot_relations(analysis, entity_labels = school_labels)
```

The middle grade contains `r length(middle_ids)` schools. Their pairwise
posterior comparisons illustrate the distinction between withholding and
similarity. Each cell in the following figure gives the expected error if
the row school were placed above the column school. Smaller values support
that direction and values near one support the reverse. The probabilities
refer to potential comparisons, independently of which comparisons the
selected grading discloses.

```{r middle-pairwise, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Directional-error probabilities for the schools in the middle grade. All remain in that same grade. Light cells can indicate a clear direction that the grade cap leaves undisclosed; the gray diagonal is excluded."}
middle_ids <- names(get_grades(analysis))[
  get_grades(analysis) == middle_grade
]
postrank_plot_pairwise(
  analysis, entities = middle_ids, ncol = 1L,
  entity_labels = school_labels, criterion_labels = criterion_labels
)
```

For example, the posterior probability that
`r unname(school_labels[strong_ids[1L]])` has lower absence than
`r unname(school_labels[strong_ids[2L]])` is
`r pct(strong_probability, 2L)`, although their comparison is withheld.
With at most `r cap` grades, disclosing an individually well-supported
comparison may require changes to other boundaries. Minimizing the combined
cost therefore accounts for both posterior uncertainty and the permitted
resolution of the report.

## Comparison of fixed reports {#compare-reports-under-the-same-choices}

We evaluate simpler reports under the same input and loss: observed-rate
tertiles, posterior-mean tertiles and a single grade withholding every
comparison. `postrank_evaluate()` calculates the risk of these supplied
grade vectors without optimizing them.

```{r fixed-actions}
fixed <- lapply(case$reference$actions, function(g) {
  postrank_evaluate(g, input,
    weights = analysis$settings$weights, tau = analysis$settings$tau)
})
```

```{r comparison-table, echo=FALSE}
evaluations <- c(list(optimized = ev), fixed)
method_names <- c(optimized = "Prepared optimized grades",
  all_withheld = "All comparisons withheld",
  observed_rate_tertiles = "Observed-rate tertiles",
  posterior_mean_tertiles = "Posterior-mean tertiles")
comparison <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(evaluations), function(method) {
  z <- evaluations[[method]]
  data.frame(Report = unname(method_names[method]),
    `Disclosed pairs` = z$N, `Expected errors` = fmt(unname(z$E), 5L),
    `Errors per disclosed pair` = if (z$N == 0) "Undefined" else pct(unname(z$E_over_N), 3L),
    Risk = fmt(z$primary_risk, 6L), check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(comparison, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "All reports use the same schools, posterior, withholding cost and grade cap. Fixed tertiles are not optimized cuts.")
```

The two tertile rules give identical grades in this subset and disclose
`r fixed$observed_rate_tertiles$N - ev$N` more pairs than the optimized report.
Their expected error count increases to
`r fmt(unname(fixed$observed_rate_tertiles$E), 3L)`, resulting in higher risk
at the stated withholding cost. This comparison is specific to the selected
schools and settings and does not establish superiority over score-based
procedures in general.

Withholding every comparison gives risk `r fmt(tau, 2L)` and undefined
`E/N`, since the number of disclosed pairs is zero. A value of zero for
`E/N` would incorrectly suggest evidence of accuracy.
[Figures and sensitivity analysis](a7-figures-sensitivity.html) considers
changes to the grade cap and withholding cost.

## Relation to the statewide analysis {#relate-the-example-to-the-statewide-study}

The statewide reference concerns `r count(state_n)` schools and
`r count(state_primary$M)` pairs. It was computed separately in the source
study. Its main procedure orders schools by posterior mean and optimizes
contiguous cuts in that fixed order. The small native optimization above
does not reproduce or establish an unrestricted statewide optimum.

```{r statewide-table, echo=FALSE}
keep <- c("posterior_mean", "raw_rate", "expected_rank", "all_tie")
state_show <- state[match(keep, state$method), ]
state_names <- c("Posterior-mean order", "Observed-rate order", "Expected-rank order",
  "All comparisons withheld")
state_table <- data.frame(Report = state_names,
  `Disclosed pairs` = count(state_show$N),
  `Disclosed fraction` = pct(state_show$N_over_M),
  `Errors per disclosed pair` = ifelse(state_show$N == 0, "Undefined", pct(state_show$E_over_N, 2L)),
  Risk = fmt(state_show$risk, 6L), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(state_table, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Archived statewide references at the same withholding cost and grade cap. Each named order uses its own optimal contiguous cuts; these are different decision problems from the small teaching subset.")
```

The posterior-mean reference discloses `r pct(state_primary$N_over_M)` of
pairs with expected errors in `r pct(state_primary$E_over_N, 2L)` of those
disclosed comparisons. Its risk is `r fmt(state_primary$risk, 6L)`. An
independent-pair relaxation gives lower bound
`r fmt(state_primary$risk_lower_bound, 6L)`, leaving a gap of
`r fmt(state_primary$absolute_relaxation_gap, 6L)`. This compares a restricted
report with a relaxation; it is not a claim that the unrestricted statewide
problem was solved. The expected-rank order has a slightly smaller stored
risk here, demonstrating that posterior-mean ordering need not yield the
lowest risk.

Numerical integration and model assumptions remain separate from either
optimization result. The primary input uses `r qcheck$order[1L]` nodes per
prior bin, with stored refinements at `r qcheck$order[2L]` and
`r qcheck$order[3L]`. The largest successive-order difference is
`r sci(max(qcheck$next_order_maximum_difference, na.rm = TRUE))`.
The source also retains small corrections of out-of-range machine-roundoff
values, separately from the public constructor's reverse-complement
symmetrization. Its primary maximum change is
`r sci(qcheck$constructor_symmetry_change[1L])`. These small changes are useful
numerical checks; neither they nor the solver gap certify the integration
error or the scientific model.

An analogous one-criterion analysis of suspension would require its own
counts, posterior and lower-rate target. Combining absence and suspension
would additionally require a specification of their relative importance.
The preparation of other single- or multi-criterion inputs is described in
[analysis of supplied posterior results](a5-your-posterior-results.html), and
result tables and files in [reading and exporting results](a6-reading-exporting-results.html).

The underlying case study is JoonHo Lee's October 2026 manuscript,
*How Much Can School Accountability Indicators Distinguish? Uncertainty-Aware
Reporting of Chronic Absenteeism and Suspension in California*. The compact
dataset records the frozen source files, model conditioning, numerical
methods and archived result qualifications in `pr_case_cde$provenance` and
`pr_case_cde$reference`.

[Posterior ranking, grades, and loss](m1-ranking-and-loss.html) develops the decision problem underlying this one-criterion report. [Posterior inputs and pairwise probabilities](m3-posterior-inputs.html) describes the information retained by the integrated probabilities and the scope of their numerical checks.
